subject: English
passage: In 2010, software engineer Xiomara Ordonez was working on converting handwritten documents into digital text. She discovered that some cursive letters were unclear enough that automatic recognition software couldn't interpret them, but most humans could easily decipher them. Based on that observation, Ordonez developed a simple verification system to distinguish real users from automated programs on websites. The initial version of her CursorGuard system asked users to identify one printed letter and one challenging cursive character that software couldn't read. Successful responses confirmed the users were human and contributed data to the handwriting recognition research.
prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To explain how recognition software operates
choices.B: To call attention to Ordonez's handwriting digitization research
choices.C: To indicate how effective CursorGuard has become
choices.D: To discuss Ordonez's invention of CursorGuard

explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it most accurately states the main purpose of the text. After providing a brief introduction to software engineer Xiomara Ordonez, the text focuses on discussing how Ordonez's digitization work led to the invention of a user verification system known as CursorGuard.
